selection.createdFor: Bodh Build Week hero journey: fraction division
selection.policy: Only canonical nodes and canonical edges needed to diagnose or teach the seeded fraction-division cases are included. Omitted upstream edges are not represented as absent knowledge.

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Dividing fractions
topics.description: Divide a fraction by a fraction using the 'keep-change-flip' method and visual models; interpret and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions
evidence: Divide a fraction by a fraction using the reciprocal method
Use visual fraction models to represent and explain fraction division
Create story contexts for fraction division problems and solve them
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has 3/4 of a litre of juice and each glass holds 3/8 of a litre, can they work out how many glasses they can fill — using fraction division?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Dividing by Fractions
topics.description: Interpret and compute division of a whole number by a unit fraction (e.g. 4 ÷ 1/5 = 20); use visual models and the relationship between multiplication and division to explain why the quotient is larger than the dividend
evidence: Compute 4 ÷ (1/5) = 20 and explain: 'How many fifths fit in 4 wholes?'
Create a story context for 6 ÷ (1/4) and solve it
Verify 4 ÷ (1/5) = 20 by showing 20 × (1/5) = 4
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you have 4 metres of ribbon and each bow needs 1/5 of a metre, can {{name}} work out how many bows you can make — and explain why the answer is bigger than 4?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Dividing fractions (unit fractions)
topics.description: Interpret and compute division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number (e.g. 1/3 ÷ 4 = 1/12); use visual models and the relationship between multiplication and division to explain the result
evidence: Compute (1/3) ÷ 4 = 1/12 and explain using a visual model of splitting 1/3 into 4 equal parts
Create a story context for (1/6) ÷ 3 and solve it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has 1/3 of a bag of rice and splits it into 4 equal portions, can they work out what fraction of the whole bag each portion is — and explain why the answer is smaller than 1/3?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Multiplying fractions (age 10+)
topics.description: Multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction, including proper fractions by proper fractions; interpret (a/b) × q as a parts of q partitioned into b equal parts; write answers in simplest form
evidence: Compute (2/3) × (4/5) = 8/15 and show with an area model
Use a visual model to demonstrate (2/3) × 4 = 8/3 = 2 2/3
Simplify the product 3/4 × 2/3 = 6/12 = 1/2
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a recipe uses 2/3 of a bag of flour and {{name}} only wants to make 3/4 of the recipe, can they multiply those fractions to find out how much flour they need?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Fractions of a whole (age 10+)
topics.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b); solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to fractional or mixed-number answers
evidence: Explain that 3/4 means 3 ÷ 4 and verify by showing 3/4 × 4 = 3
Solve: '9 people share a 50-pound sack equally — how many pounds each?' and express the answer as 5 5/9
Use a visual model to show that sharing 3 wholes among 4 people gives each person 3/4
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} shares 3 pizzas equally among 4 friends, can they work out what fraction each person gets — and explain why 3 ÷ 4 gives the same answer as 3/4?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Multiplying fractions
topics.description: Understand a/b as a multiple of 1/b; multiply proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers, supported by visual models (e.g. 3 × 2/5 = 6/5 = 1 1/5)
evidence: Calculate 4 × 3/8 using repeated addition or the rule n × a/b = (n×a)/b
Multiply 2 1/3 × 3 and express as a mixed number
Use a visual model to show why 5 × 1/4 = 5/4
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a recipe uses 2/3 of a cup of butter and {{name}} wants to make it three times over, can they work out how much butter they need in total?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Understanding fractions (age 9+)
topics.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b (e.g. 3/5 = 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5)
evidence: Express 5/8 as a sum of five copies of 1/8
Show on a number line how 4/3 is built by iterating 1/3 four times
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} to show 4/5 as a sum of smaller equal fractions, can they write it out as 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Fractions of a whole
topics.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a/b as a parts of size 1/b
evidence: Given a shape divided into 5 equal parts, identify one shaded part as 1/5
Explain that 3/4 means 3 parts each of size 1/4
Draw a model showing 2/6 as 2 pieces of a whole cut into 6
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you cut a pizza into 6 equal slices, can {{name}} explain what 1/6 means — and then work out what 4/6 of the pizza looks like?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: Division as Unknown Factor
topics.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem (e.g. find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8)
evidence: Explain that 32 ÷ 8 = ? is the same as 8 × ? = 32
Use a known multiplication fact to find a division answer
Describe the relationship between multiplication and division as inverse operations
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out '32 ÷ 8' by asking 'what do I multiply 8 by to get 32?' — using times table knowledge rather than a separate division method?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: What Division Means
topics.description: Interpret whole-number quotients (e.g. 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share or the number of equal groups)
evidence: Explain that 56 ÷ 8 can mean sharing 56 into 8 equal groups or making groups of 8
Draw a picture to represent a division expression
Match a division expression to a word problem involving equal sharing or grouping
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that '56 ÷ 8' could mean 'if 56 things are shared between 8 people, how many does each person get?' — not just recite the answer '7'?

dependencies.reason: Dividing fractions uses the reciprocal method which builds on fraction multiplication
Dividing fraction by fraction extends Y5 dividing unit fractions by whole numbers
Understanding fraction as division supports reasoning about quotients
Whole ÷ unit-fraction uses inverse relationship with fraction multiplication
Understanding unit-fraction ÷ whole helps contrast with whole ÷ unit-fraction
Understanding fraction as division supports interpreting 1/3 ÷ 4
Unit-fraction ÷ whole uses inverse relationship with fraction multiplication
Fraction × fraction extends Y5 fraction × whole number
Understanding fraction as division builds on fraction × whole number (inverse reasoning)
a/b as sum of 1/b is prerequisite to understanding a/b as multiple of 1/b
Understanding a/b as a parts of size 1/b is prerequisite to understanding a/b as sum of 1/b
Seeing division as unknown-factor requires understanding division first
